To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we provide a prediction based approach for quantifying the additional uncertainty that is caused by a mismatch of the model, and (ii) we show that the Kullback–Leibler rate divergence is a natural metric for this problem.

(1) the variance based approach is equivalent to the classical BODE formula in control theory, (2) the Kullback-Liebler divergence based approach is equivalent, in the case of scalar systems, to a recently introduced notion of “information distance” in information theory, and (3) the two approaches are different in the multivariate case.

the variance based metric is a special case of the Kull-back-Leibler divergence based metric, the variance based metric does not capture all information about the extra uncertainty, and the Kullback- Liebler divergence based metric is more informative than the variance based metric, and is more suitable for comparing two systems.

the Kullback Leibler metric is more suitable than the variance based metric in the case of a linear model and an unknown input, while the opposite is true for a nonlinear model and a known input.

the Kullback-Liebler metric is a better metric than the variance based metric in terms of its robustness.
